title: Requires AND Ensures Together
story: A function with only `requires` checks inputs but not outputs. A function with only `ensures` checks outputs but not inputs. But a truly safe function needs BOTH: validate what comes in AND verify what goes out. When you combine `requires` AND `ensures`, you create a complete contract — a function that can't be called wrong AND can't return wrong.
why: Combining requires and ensures creates a complete specification — the function is guarded on both sides, catching bad inputs at the call site and bad outputs at the return site.
analogy: A full contract (requires + ensures) is like a bank's safe deposit box procedure. Before accessing the box, you must show valid ID (requires: id is valid). The bank verifies this at the entrance. When you return the box, the bank inspects it to confirm the contents are correct (ensures: box contents match log). Both sides of the transaction are verified. If either check fails, the process halts — no exceptions.
try_it: Write `safe_modulo(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int` with both requires and ensures. Add `requires: b != 0;` and `ensures: result >= 0;` and `ensures: result < b;` (assuming positive b). Then add `requires: b > 0;` to simplify the ensures. Write a `saturating_add(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int` that doesn't overflow — with `ensures: result >= a;` and `ensures: result >= b;`. Test with very large numbers. What ensures can you write for `saturating_sub`?
tips: Write requires first (what must be true going in), then ensures (what must be true coming out)
The ensures often depends on the requires being true — you can assume requires holds when writing ensures
A complete contract often makes the function body trivial — the contract IS the documentation
common_mistakes: Writing `ensures: result > 0;` when the requires doesn't guarantee it — if balance can be 0, result could be 0
Making ensures too weak — `ensures: result >= 0;` is true but doesn't actually verify the withdrawal math
Forgetting that ensures uses `result`, NOT the variable name you assign the return value to inside the function
